entries.text: Klemperer’s Philharmonia Matthew Passion is the monumental modern studio reading: slow from the first chorus, star opera and lieder cast, large choir with boys’ ripieno. Against Gardiner’s period Archiv set it is the opposite stance — opera-house weight rather than workshop clarity. Tempo remains contested; the cast still justifies the disc. The modern monument, not the Référence on this cut.

Gardiner’s 1988 Archiv Matthew Passion restored the work to period instruments and a tighter drama after the large modern monuments. The Monteverdi Choir and English Baroque Soloists play with theatrical sense; Rolfe Johnson and Schmidt hold the narrative clean. Against Klemperer’s Philharmonia epic it is the other stance — workshop clarity rather than opera-house weight. Référence for the HIP studio side: start here if that is the approach you want.
